proposal: Add "beach volleyball" to the sport enum in scripts/config/registry.schema.json so the world-registry vocabulary matches catalog.json's entity vocabulary. The registry schema's own sport field is documented as "samme vokabular som catalog.json", and catalog.schema.json's tier2 entity sport enum DOES include "beach volleyball" (Mol/Sørum live in catalog.json tier2.athletes with sport:"beach volleyball"), but registry.schema.json's enum was missing it — silently rejecting any attempt to register those entities. Also added a coherence test (tests/registry-schema.test.js) that pins the registry sport enum to be a superset of catalog.schema.json's entity sport enum, so this drift can never silently return.
evidence: research-log 2026-10-19 (deep-tier Monday sweep), note 'STEP 2.8 REGISTRY-SVEIP': 'FUNN for improve: Mol/Sørum (catalog.tier2) kan IKKE legges i registeret — registry.schema.json mangler «beach volleyball» i sport-enumet.' The research agent (the registry's weekly maintainer) hit this blocker directly.

scripts/config/catalog.json tier2.athletes lines 48–49: Anders Mol and Christian Sørum both carry sport:"beach volleyball" — Norwegian Olympic/5x-European champions, added at WP-116 (2026-08-11 horizon scan).

scripts/config/catalog.schema.json line 59 (the tier2 entity sport enum) INCLUDES "beach volleyball"; registry.schema.json's entity sport enum (line matching the tier1 list, 14 values) did NOT — a documented-vocabulary drift, since the registry schema description claims the same vocabulary as catalog.json.

npm test: 88 files / 1546 tests pass (+2 new in tests/registry-schema.test.js: registry sport enum covers every catalog entity sport; includes beach volleyball). No registry file changes — purely additive to the enum, so every existing registry file still validates byte-identically.
expectedEffect: The research/improve agents can register Anders Mol and Christian Sørum (and any future beach-volleyball entity) in the world registry with stable ids, so they resolve in app/web search and entity matching instead of being blocked by a schema the vocabulary contract says should accept them. The grader's recurring flag about this long-tail gap clears once the entities are seeded.
howWeKnow: The next registry maintenance run can add beach-volleyball entities without a schema-validation failure; the new coherence test keeps the registry enum in lockstep with catalog.schema.json's entity enum going forward.
notes: Smallest viable change: one enum value + a coherence test. Purely additive — no registry data file changed, so no re-seed/diff.
